news.title: Bompastor on latest team news and needing to be at our best against Hacken
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor feels that Tuesday night's UEFA Women's Champions League fixture against Hacken has come at exactly the right time to help Chelsea shake off Saturday's disappointing 1-1 draw with Everton in domestic action. The stalemate with the Toffees saw Sandy Baltimore put us in front with a header, but an unfortunate own goal from Lucy Bronze levelled the scores. And despite our best efforts in the second half, we couldn't put ourselves back in front. There's little time between Saturday afternoon's final whistle and Tuesday's 5.45pm kick-off (UK time) in Gothenburg, but Bompastor feels that it will be good to get back out on the pitch quickly to shake off the result against Everton. And aside from Naomi Girma and Lauren James, who were not part of the travelling squad, the head coach confirmed she has a full complement to pick from. 'All the other players are fit and available,' said Bompastor, before going on to discuss our impressive record in the Champions League, in which we have not conceded a single goal in our opening three league phase encounters. 'It’s important for us to stay in that good form, especially on the back of a disappointing result at the weekend. 'In this competition we also have ambitions, and right now we are in the top four. That’s the goal: we want to be in the top four and stay there. So we want to put in a good performance and get a good result tomorrow. Staying strong defensively, not conceding too much and keeping a clean sheet would be a good thing.' In a match where we had 65 per cent possession and fired 20 shots towards goal against Everton, the head coach said she was frustrated not to take all three points. But football moves on quickly, and Bompastor wants to take the opportunity to put in an improved display against Hacken. 'I think the frustration came from the result because we have ambitions, and dropping two points at home is never good, but it happens. The good thing with a quick turnaround is you analyse the game and give the players feedback, but you also need to move on. You need to focus on something new. We have a new game coming, in a new competition, so it’s the best thing for us in terms of moving on.' Hacken were crowned Swedish champions for the second year running last week, and won the inaugural Women’s Europa Cup last season. However, their Champions League campaign has been tougher, with defeats to Inter and Juventus followed by a 1-1 draw away at Paris FC, secured by a 93rd-minute equaliser. Bompastor believes those results haven’t reflected Hacken’s performances, and she warned of the threats they carry. 'Hacken's Champions League results didn’t necessarily reflect their performances on the pitch,' Bompastor explained. 'They have strengths and threats, especially in the attacking line, with speed and pace. So we will have to be really careful in the transitional moments of the game. 'For me, it’s important we find the right balance between focusing on ourselves and making sure we don’t give them many opportunities. They are playing at home, so they’ll want a good result, and we need to be at our best tomorrow.'

news.title: Chelsea Women's Constant Contact October Goal of the Month revealed!
news.body_en: Maika Hamano's sublime strike against Tottenham Hotspur in the Women's Super League has been voted as our Constant Contact Goal of the Month for October! Hamano came on after half-time against Spurs, and she marked her appearance against her former loan club with a stunning swerving effort from almost 30 yards out. The replays showed just how much the ball moved once it had left her foot, and the goal certainly got the Blues fans off their seats at Stamford Bridge. Her strike was the clear winner among Blues fans, receiving 60 per cent of all votes cast. Lauren James' superb effort in the same game against Spurs at the Bridge finished second with 16 per cent, while Melvine Malard's shot from range against Crystal Palace received nine per cent and was ranked in third place.

news.title: Chelsea Women vs Hacken: How to watch, TV channel, kick-off time, date
news.body_en: Chelsea's UEFA Women's Champions League campaign continues as we travel to Sweden to face Hacken on Tuesday evening. The Blues are unbeaten in Europe this season and are yet to concede after three matches of the league phase. We will be looking for our first away win of the campaign as the Champions League returns to the top of the agenda in midweek. Here is everything you need to know about how to watch Hacken against Chelsea Women, including kick-off time and how to follow the action on official Chelsea channels. Chelsea Women's game against Hacken takes place on Tuesday 10 November at Hisingen Arena, with kick-off scheduled for 5.45pm UK time (6.45pm local time). The match will be shown live in the UK on Disney+. As always, you can follow minute-by-minute updates in our Hacken vs Chelsea Match Centre on the Chelsea Official App and website. You can also follow through Chelsea Women’s social media channels on X, Facebook and Instagram. Chelsea are yet to lose or concede in this season's Champions League, beating Austria Vienna 1-0 and Roma 2-0 at Plough Lane, either side of a goalless draw away at Lyon. That run has extended our record-breaking unbeaten streak in league phase and group stage fixtures to 27 games. Hacken, last season's Women's Europa Cup winners, arrive as newly crowned Damallsvenskan champions, having lost just once in 25 league games. However, in Europe, they are still looking for a first win, with defeats to Inter and Juventus followed by a 1-1 draw away at Paris FC. Chelsea are unbeaten in two previous meetings with Hacken, both in the group stage of the 2023/24 Women's Champions League. A goalless draw at Stamford Bridge was followed six days later by a 3-1 win in Gothenburg, with a goal from Sam Kerr and an Erin Cuthbert brace.

news.title: Xabi Alonso calls for consistency after ‘ups and downs’
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso knows there were positives and negatives from his Chelsea team’s performances since the October international break, but wants to see the Blues hitting our top level more consistently when we return from the latest one. We enter the November break – the last of this year, with the next interruption to the club football schedule not arriving until March 2027 – off the back of a loss, as a first-half penalty condemned us to a narrow 1-0 defeat away at Sunderland on Sunday. That is a repeat of the previous international window, in late September and early October, when we were beaten at Brentford in our final game leading into the break. Since then, results have been mixed. Strong wins over Bournemouth, Everton and Manchester United – bringing our first two Premier League clean sheets of the season in the process – were offset by our exit from the Carabao Cup in a penalty shoot-out at Liverpool and league defeats to Tottenham Hotspur and, now, Sunderland. It was that inconsistency in league results and performance which was on our manager’s mind when he was asked for his opinion on how this run of fixtures has gone for the Blues. ‘Three wins, two defeats, it could have been better,’ reflected Alonso. ‘It’s progress, but we want to be more consistent. ‘It was about finishing this block with a good feeling but, like the last block against Brentford, we lost. ‘For sure, it’s ups and downs, and we are still missing that consistency that is needed in the Premier League.' The good news is that Alonso, his staff, and those members of his squad who aren’t heading away to join their national teams in the coming days, now have time to plan and prepare to put that right in time for the Premier League’s return. That comes on Saturday 21 November, when Chelsea will host old rivals Leeds United at Stamford Bridge. We will be looking to get straight back to winning ways after this international break, just as we did last time around by thrashing Bournemouth 5-1 in west London on our return to the pitch. ‘The plan is to use the time with the players we have,’ Xabi added on his plans for the international break. ‘Some players will go on international duties, but we keep working.’

news.title: Mike Penders focused on ‘staying together’ after difficult Sunderland defeat
news.body_en: Mike Penders did not hide from the disappointment and frustration felt in the Chelsea dressing room after Sunday’s loss at Sunderland. A tight contest at the Stadium of Light was decided by Enzo Le Fee’s first-half penalty. The Blues enjoyed plenty of possession and territory, especially after the break, but couldn’t create clear opportunities against a resolute Black Cats rearguard. Besides one outstanding save in the second period to deny Wilson Isidor, Penders didn’t have a great deal to do, either. But the damage had been done and one goal proved enough for Sunderland’s second league win of the season. ‘Very disappointed with the result,’ Penders said. ‘You know when you come here to their stadium that it will be a difficult game, and they fought very hard. ‘At one point, it went very fast from side to side. Sometimes we had control and, of course, in certain moments when you go higher up the pitch they will be very aggressive and the way they play is very difficult. ‘In the second half they dropped very low and had every man behind the ball, so we had a bit more control and we had to push. We had some chances, but it was difficult against 11 behind the ball to find the right spaces. We kept pushing, especially in the last 15 minutes, we kept dropping balls at them, but it wasn’t enough.’ With domestic action pausing for the international break, there is now a brief window to reset before we host Leeds on 21 November. For Penders, the key now is maintaining collective belief and building on the positive elements of recent performances ahead of our return to action later this month. ‘If you watch some of the last games, we played pretty well,’ said Penders. ‘The structure is getting better and it’s a pity that we have lost this game. ‘It’s a matter of staying together. I think we’ve had some good games, but after losing these games, we have to stick together. It’s the international break now, so we can calm our heads, and when we come back we need to all be motivated and go again.’

Full Match: Sunderland vs Chelsea
Extended: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea
Alonso: 'Not happy with the performance or result'
Highlights: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea
Alonso: We didn’t produce enough to deserve to win
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso felt the Blues could have come away from Sunderland with a point with a bit more luck, but accepted we didn’t do enough to deserve more than that. We succumbed to a narrow 1-0 defeat at the Stadium of Light in a game ultimately decided by one first-half refereeing decision, which saw the home side awarded a first-half penalty that Enzo Le Fee converted. The Blues pushed hard for an equaliser to salvage a point in the second period, especially during the closing stages, when substitutes Geovany Quenda and Danny Welbeck both went close. However, Alonso was in no mood to make excuses after the final whistle, admitting his side hadn’t performed at the level he expects, particularly when it came to our attempts to break down the stubborn Sunderland defence after falling behind. ‘I would say there were situations that we could have defended better, situations that we could have got better advantages in attack, but the game was really even, really competitive,’ said our manager. ‘They were waiting for the chance – and they got it. After they took the lead, we were trying, but we were not producing much. The first goal is always important and today, when we were behind, we didn't produce enough. ‘It wasn't the best game. I think that we didn't deserve more than probably one point. The game was really close. ‘Not much happened, to be honest, just that action [for the Sunderland penalty]. We had the cross in the first half, the header from Morgan (Rogers), but we didn't produce enough to deserve to win. ‘We were against a low block. We missed a bit of patience and a bit of quality, creativity in the last third to create more chances. You need to be more consistent to move the ball from one side to the other, and we didn't do good enough.’ Alonso conceded that the absences of unavailable players could have influenced our performance, as Josh Acheampong was ruled out with a small issue on Saturday and the game was too soon for Emiliano Martinez to make his return. Jorrel Hato, Jamie Gittens, Reece James, Maxence Lacroix and Joao Pedro also remain out. The Blues will now go into the international break hoping to get at least some of those players back for our next game against Leeds United on 21 November, even if Alonso made clear he expects better from the Blues, whoever is in the team. ‘There are situations,' he acknowledged. 'Yesterday Josh felt something and he was not fit to play. So we are shorter in options and we need to go through this time. ‘Even when we win, or when we lose, we miss some players that we have injured and for sure we are waiting to have them back because they are important. Now we need to use the time to recover them, but with the players we have, we have to get ready for the next one.’

news.title: Match report: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea fell to a narrow defeat at the Stadium of Light on Sunday as a first-half penalty secured Sunderland the points. We could easily have had a spot-kick of our own before Enzo Le Fee netted the only goal, with a foul on Cole Palmer adjudged to have taken place just outside the box. The margins were fine in a scrappy contest, and another decision went the home side’s way after Brian Brobbey and Levi Colwill came together in the box. Le Fee converted. Having led at half-time for the first time this season, Sunderland defended their advantage doggedly. We struggled to fashion clear chances, with the best headed over by sub Danny Welbeck in stoppage time. Xabi Alonso made a pair of changes to the team that started against Manchester United last weekend. Pep Chavarria came in for Josh Acheampong, who missed out entirely with what Alonso said was a ‘minor issue’. Further forward, Jordan Henderson returned at the club where he came through, with Estevao Willian making way. Henderson played as the most advanced of a midfield trio also containing Moises Caicedo and Romeo Lavia. Mike Penders continued in goal, with Emiliano Martinez deemed not quite ready to start after his jaw surgery. There was also a place on the bench for Aaron Anselmino for the first time this season. After an immaculately observed period of silence to mark Remembrance Sunday, play got underway with Chelsea defending the goal high behind which the 3,000-strong travelling support were housed. Our hosts were dealt an early blow when Granit Xhaka had to be withdrawn inside four minutes. A scrappy start was punctured by a good chance for Brobbey, who volleyed Chemsdine Talbi’s teasing cross wide from close range. Midway through the half, Palmer was chopped down by Luke O’Nien as he advanced into the box. The referee didn’t give a foul, but replays showed it clearly was one. The only question was whether it took place inside the box. It was a very tight call, and one that unfortunately didn’t go in our favour. We very nearly let out our frustrations at that decision by immediately taking the lead. An inviting cross by Palestra from the right flank was met by the rising Rogers, who couldn’t steer his header on target. Brobbey was proving a nuisance. He led a breakaway from Colwill inside his own half but Fofana did well to take him wide. When the shot arrived, it flew over the bar. However, there was no such reprieve on 35 minutes. Brobbey spun Colwill and having got the wrong side of our defender, went to ground. There wasn’t a lot in it, with both players having a hold of the other’s shirt, but the referee’s on-call decision of penalty stood. Le Fee sent Penders the wrong way from 12 yards. It stayed 1-0 until half-time and Alonso responded by bringing on Estevao for Colwill. Caicedo dropped back into central defence, and we now had another attacker on the pitch. With the Blues still finding time and space in the final third at a premium, Alonso made two more changes on the hour. Welbeck and Malo Gusto replaced Neto and Palestra, with the Frenchman making his 100th Premier League appearance. There were a couple of nearly moments for first Estevao and then Palmer as a pair of penetrative passes from Rogers prized the Sunderland backline open. With 15 to play, it needed a brave and big save from Penders to deny Wilson Isidor – not long on for Brobbey – after a loose ball fell to him six yards out. Geovany Quenda nearly scored with his first involvement, a left-footed strike that took a deflection and had Robin Roefs scrambling across his goal. There was plenty of late possession and territory for the Blues, and the chance to equalise came from the head of Welbeck in stoppage time. Unfortunately, his effort flew over the bar, and with it went our hopes of returning to London with something to show for our efforts. We go into the final international break of the season in fifth place in the Premier League table. The Blues host Leeds United on Saturday 21 November following the pause for international football. news.title: Premier League 2 report: Tottenham Hotspur 1-3 Chelsea Cobham Next Gen
news.body_en: Chelsea Cobham Next Gen leapfrogged Tottenham Hotspur into second in the Premier League 2 table after a Harrison McMahon goal and a brace from Chizaram Ezenwata sealed a 3-1 win. It didn’t take the Blues long to take the lead, with McMahon scoring his second goal in as many matches by rounding goalkeeper Samual Archer and finishing after being put through one-on-one by Reggie Watson. Ezenwata doubled our advantage before the interval with his seventh goal of the season across all competitions for the Blues. We defended well for much of the second period, but Spurs pulled a goal back with 14 minutes to play when James Rowswell found the net. Despite late pressure from the hosts, we made sure of all three points when Ezenwata struck his second in stoppage time to seal victory. We exploited Tottenham’s high backline from the off, and Sol Gordon had an opportunity inside five minutes. A good ball forward from Calvin Diakite put the Blues winger through, but Archer saved well to turn the ball behind for a corner. It proved only a momentary reprieve for the home side as we soon broke the deadlock. Watson played a long ball over the top to McMahon, who remained composed to take the ball around the goalkeeper and slot home. We continued to probe the Tottenham defence across the remainder of the opening 45 minutes, although the hosts had chances of their own and Freddy Bernal produced a couple of smart stops in the Chelsea goal. Shortly before the interval, Gordon again came close. The Blues winger beat the Spurs' offside trap, raced into the box and aimed a shot toward the far post. Gordon's attempt beat Archer but was cleared off the line, and while Leo Cardoso was there for the follow-up, he was also denied. Three minutes before the interval, however, our second arrived. It was somewhat straightforward as Bernal hit a long pass into the Tottenham half and Ezenwata manoeuvred his way beyond the last defender and confidently finished beyond Archer. After the break, we kept pushing and came close to extending our advantage from corners, with Olutayo Subuloye asserting his dominance in the penalty area. Corners from Watson found the head of Subuloye repeatedly, with the Blues skipper consistently overpowering his marker, but he couldn't divert his attempts on target. Ezenwata also came close, utilising his excellent hold-up play to manufacture an opportunity. The Chelsea striker had his back to goal when he received possession, but created half a yard to get his shot off. Unfortunately, it curled too late and went just wide of the far post. Tottenham’s skipper, Roswell, halved the deficit from a set piece with 76 minutes left on the clock. Yet it was the Blues who had the final say in this derby. As the game entered additional time, Tottenham earned a free kick which they opted to take quickly. Substitute Harrison Bettoni reacted quickest to intercept the ball and get a shot away. His attempt was too powerful for Archer, who palmed the ball back out to Ezenwata. The Blues striker made no mistake and thumped a shot into the back of the net to put the game to bed and ensure all three points returned to Cobham. Our 3-1 win on derby day means that we are up to 16 points in PL2 after seven matches. We have leapfrogged Spurs and now sit in second position. Cobham Next Gen are back in PL2 action on Friday 27 November following the international break, when we face Norwich City at the Avant Training Centre. The game gets underway at 7pm GMT and supporters can watch the match live with a CFC+ subscription. news.title: Alonso explains Acheampong and Martinez absences against Sunderland
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has explained why Josh Acheampong and Emi Martinez are not in the Chelsea squad for today's game against Sunderland, which the Blues manager says will be a tough and intense contest. Our final fixture before the November international break takes us to the Stadium of Light, where we will face a Sunderland side that has won one of their opening nine top-flight matches. The Blues' last outing was a 2-0 victory over Manchester United at Stamford Bridge. Alonso has made two changes to the side that started that win, with Pep Chavarria replacing Acheampong in defence and Jordan Henderson coming in for Estevao Willian. Alonso was asked ahead of this afternoon's contest why Acheampong wasn't included in the matchday squad. He replied: ‘He is recovering from a minor thing. 'He missed the fitness to be ready for today but we are expecting that he will be back after the international break. It’s a pity because he was in a good moment.’ Martinez hasn't featured for the Blues since our win at Everton last month. The Argentine goalkeeper had to undergo jaw surgery following the victory due to a collision with Jarrad Branthwaite. The 34-year-old returned to training this week wearing protective headgear but wasn't quite ready to take his place in the squad. Alonso said: ‘He has made a great effort to be available but probably it was too rash, too risky [to be selected]. So he will use one more week, ten days, to keep on training and get used to the mask. I’m sure after the break he will be available.’ Henderson's return to the Blues' starting XI comes in the city he was born in – and against the club he started his career with. Alonso is confident the England international will once again bring plenty to our midfield against a tough opponent. He added: ‘No, I remember his start here in Sunderland, it’s not that he plays because he was born here, it’s because he is so important for the team and is doing really well. I’m sure he is going to help today. ‘All the games in the Premier League are tough, we know that even when you play well you maybe don’t get what you deserve, but this is the reality of the Premier League. For sure it’s going to be a tough game for both sides, intense, but we feel ready and hopefully we can finish with a good win before the internationals.’

Why Xabi Alonso wants 'busy weeks' in his Chelsea future
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso and his Chelsea players have had seven days to prepare for today's trip to Sunderland. However, the Blues manager does not want that luxury next season. With no European football on our agenda this term, Alonso has enjoyed more quality time with his squad on the training pitches at Cobham during the opening months of his tenure. That has been important for the Spaniard, who is still embedding his tactical principles and forging close bonds with his players. He has overseen a largely positive start to the campaign, with the Blues fourth in the top flight having taken 16 points from our opening nine fixtures. Our tenth takes place this afternoon as we travel to Sunderland, who, in contrast to the Blues, are competing in European football for the first time in more than 50 years. That comes with its own pressures and a more punishing schedule. Yet it's one Alonso wants  – and one he insists he and his players are working toward. 'The ambition is to be back there [in Europe],' the Blues manager explained during his pre-match press conference. '[We want it] to be just one season that we are having long weeks. The aim, the desire, the hunger is to have busy weeks, to have to deal with three games a week, and that we'll see each other much more. 'It's not that it hurts now, because you deal with it, but this is where we want to be.' As a two-time Champions League winner and someone who made 119 appearances in the competition during his playing career, Alonso is well-versed in the demands that come with performing at the top table of European football. He wants Chelsea to be back on that stage, but appreciates that only comes through hard work and consistency in the months ahead. 'We want to be playing in Europe, in big stadiums, having top teams in Europe because I think that we can be there, but we need to earn it to be there. 'We like football and, unfortunately, we can only comment [on what has taken place during a European gameweek]. The feeling is that we want to be there, but we need to deserve that.'

news.title: Opposition scout – Sunderland
news.body_en: Ahead of Chelsea's Premier League meeting with Sunderland, we take a closer look at the Black Cats, their approach under Regis Le Bris and the players who could make an impact. The Black Cats are 12 points shy of last season’s tally at the same stage, having scored four fewer goals and conceded ten more. While many of their metrics are comparable to last season, Regis Le Bris’s team have been affected by individual errors, with three of their players having made mistakes that twice led to goals. Le Bris, who joined the Wearsiders from French club Lorient in 2024, has maintained a consistent line-up from last season despite plenty of investment over recent transfer windows. Nine of Sunderland’s starters in the 3-0 loss to Coventry last weekend began the match in May at Stamford Bridge that clinched their first European foray since 1973 at Chelsea’s expense. The Frenchman has handled Sunderland’s busy schedule by making substantial changes in cup games at home and abroad. The workload may also explain a more measured approach to high pressing – they have not scored from a high turnover this season. The manager will be forced into at least one change in central defence, as Luke O’Nien’s partner Omar Alderete is suspended after receiving a second yellow card in the last minute at Coventry. Le Bris has stuck with the midfield pivot of Granit Xhaka, now 34, and Noah Sadiki, and often prefers full-backs such as Trai Hume or Thomas Meunier on the wings over the likes of summer signings Jocelin Ta Bi and Malick Fofana. Lone striker and leading marksman Brian Brobbey has accounted for three of Sunderland’s seven league goals, one ahead of No.10 Enzo Le Fee. Centre-back Dan Ballard, midfielder Habib Diarra and winger Romaine Mundle are injured, but left-back Nordi Mukiele and teenage striker Juan Riquelme Angulo could return to readiness.

news.body_en: It was on this day in 1996, precisely 30 years ago now, that the Blues completed the signing of Gianfranco Zola, who over seven seasons at Stamford Bridge stole the hearts of Chelsea fans everywhere. He helped win four trophies and scored the winner in the 1998 European Cup Winners' Cup final just seconds after coming on as substitute. In all, Franco scored 80 goals in 312 games, with many of them being spectacular efforts. You can watch the lot below!Goals that will live long in the memory include a mid-air back-flick against Norwich City, an effort against Manchester United that left opposition goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel motionless and a brilliant turn and shot in a 1997 FA Cup semi-final win over Wimbledon. Above all, Franco always played football as if he enjoyed it and was almost universally popular amongst opposition fans.Zola did suffer a dip in form during the 2001/02 season but returned strongly the following season, scoring 16 times as we qualified for the Champions League. He scored his last goal for Chelsea on Easter Monday 2003 and in his final appearance came on for the last 20 minutes of a win over Liverpool that saw us claim fourth place and with it, Champions League qualification. It was a truly fitting finale to a glorious Chelsea career.

news.title: Gianfranco Zola’s greatest moments in Blue
news.body_en: Gianfranco Zola is, quite simply, one of Chelsea’s very best. On the 30th anniversary of his signing, what better time to relive Zola’s glorious career in west London. The Italian magician arrived from Parma on 8 November 1996 and left nearly seven years later as an all-time great, his place in our history books cemented by a catalogue of indelible moments. Narrowing them down to a shortlist is no easy feat – anybody who had the good fortune of watching Zola play for us will call to mind different memories of his genius. But here are 11 moments, in chronological order, that we think stand out above the rest... Zola’s first Chelsea goal was a sign of things to come. Standing over a free-kick 35 yards out, few would have given him a chance of finding the net – but we didn’t know then quite how capable he was from set-pieces. His strike had whip and dip, leaving Everton’s keeper Neville Southall and a defender who had hastily retreated to the line in a spin, and Chelsea mouths agape. A fortnight later Zola’s ingenuity again left Stamford Bridge in awe. This time he was released down the right-hand channel before turning grizzled West Ham full-back Julian Dicks inside and out and firing home with aplomb. 'I didn't know who Julian Dicks was at that point,' Gianfranco joked years later. 'Probably if I had known maybe I wouldn't have done that as it was too dangerous!' Few made the great Manchester United team of the nineties and noughties look as silly as Zola did in just the second minute of a February ’97 Premier League meeting. He first cut inside the sliding Dennis Irwin before easing past Gary Pallister, left imbalanced by Zola’s delicate touch. The finish that followed was emphatic, fired past the rooted Peter Schmeichel at his near post. Not even six months into his Chelsea career and Zola had already accumulated an enviable collection of wonder goals. Arguably none topped his dazzling effort in the FA Cup semi-final win over Wimbledon at Highbury. Running adjacent to the goal, Zola collected a pass from Roberto Di Matteo and with his first touch somehow flicked it back in the opposite direction and into his path as he shifted his weight. One more touch and then bang – the ball was in the Wimbledon net! Zola’s debut season in England captured the attention of fans and pundits alike, to the extent the country’s journalists voted him as their Football Writers’ Association Footballer of the Year by a distance – Zola polled twice the number of votes gained by Juninho and our own Mark Hughes. It was a season in which he also scored the winning goal for Italy against England at Wembley. Our first piece of major silverware in a generation was secured when Eddie Newton forced the ball home from close range late on in our FA Cup final triumph against Middlesbrough at Wembley. The goal owed much to the majesty of Zola, who deftly flicked Dan Petrescu’s cross back into the six-yard box for Newton to convert. Zola’s most famous Chelsea goal arrived scarcely 20 seconds after he had entered the action in the 1998 Cup Winners’ Cup final. He wasted no time making an impact, latching on a Dennis Wise pass and thrashing the ball high into the roof of the net. It was his most famous Chelsea goal and it won us the Cup Winners’ Cup. Our first ever Champions League quarter-final tie paired us with the might of Barcelona. Zola inspired an extraordinary performance with a trademark free-kick that dipped over the wall and into the Shed End net. We were 3-0 up by the break at an ecstatic Stamford Bridge in what will go down as one of Chelsea’s greatest halves of football ever. Not many goals leave people speechless, but Zola managed just that in an FA Cup tie against Norwich in 2002. He met Graeme Le Saux’s low corner on the full with a backflicked volley that fizzed past Rob Green in a flash. It wasn’t until the replay was shown on the big screen at Stamford Bridge that the audacity and execution of the finish was evident. Zola finished as he started. Just as his first Chelsea goal had the Bridge faithful in awe, so did his last. With Chelsea cruising against Everton in our quest to finish in the top four, Zola raced down the left and, from an improbable angle, lofted the bouncing ball over Richard Wright in the Everton goal. It was the kind of moment of magic Zola had deservedly earned a reputation as producing on a regular basis. Zola’s final game for the Blues was a huge one as we hosted Liverpool at the Bridge with the final spot in the Champions League places up for grabs. We led 2-1 when Zola came off the bench and, with time ticking down, danced between a gaggle of red shirts, including a bewildered Jamie Carragher, in a clip that has stood the test of time to go viral in the modern age. It epitomised his genius. When Zola met Carragher... ✨ pic.twitter.com/3Dpxv9VSIE

Five of Chelsea's most memorable moments against Sunderland
news.body_en: Sunderland may have only been an opponent of ours in just over half of the Premier League seasons to date, but the Black Cats have been on the receiving end of some iconic Chelsea moments. We first played Sunderland in the Premier League in 1996/97, recording a memorable 6-2 victory at Stamford Bridge. Since then, there have been goals, performances and top-flight title celebrations that will live long in the memory. Here we bring you the top five… Chelsea 4-0 Sunderland7 August 1999 The sun was shining at Stamford Bridge as Chelsea, tipped for the title by some, started the new season in style by sinking newly-promoted Sunderland. Gus Poyet, Gianfranco Zola and Tore Andre Flo had already given us an unassailable lead when Poyet bagged the goal of the game. Zola scooped the ball over the Mackems’ defence and into the path of Poyet, who expertly scissor-kicked his volley into the top corner. In creation and execution, it was simply sublime. Chelsea 7-2 Sunderland16 January 2010 In a season full of goals, Ashley Cole’s against Sunderland at the turn of the year was voted by supporters as the best, and it was easy to see why. From inside his own half, John Terry put a lofted first-time pass into the path of the marauding left-back. Running at full tilt didn’t stop Cole bringing the ball under his spell with an immaculate first touch. As Sunderland skipper Lorik Cana slid across to block the shot, Cole calmly cut the ball inside him before using the outside of his left boot to find the far corner. Sunderland 3-4 Chelsea4 December 2013 Singling out one Eden Hazard performance for Chelsea is no easy task, but his display at the Stadium of Light in December 2013 arguably stands above the rest. After providing an assist for Frank Lampard, Hazard netted two individual goals of the highest quality to help us to a 4-3 win. His second goal, again after combining with Lampard, was particularly magical. He instinctively and ecstatically ripped off his shirt in celebration, a sure sign even the cool Belgian was impressed by his masterclass on Wearside. Chelsea 3-1 Sunderland24 May 2015 Both of our most recent Premier League trophy lifts have come after final-day victories over Sunderland at Stamford Bridge. The first was in May 2015, when a penalty from Diego Costa and a Loic Remy brace secured a 3-1 success after we had gone behind early. One of the many highlights that day was the sight of Didier Drogba being carried off the pitch by his team-mates after his final Chelsea appearance. History would repeat itself two years later… Chelsea 5-1 SunderlandMay 21 2017 On that occasion, it was John Terry who was celebrated off the Stamford Bridge turf 26 minutes into his final game, which would prove a resounding victory over the relegated Black Cats. Again, we went behind. Again, we hit back in style. Willian levelled with an angle finish before goals from Eden Hazard and Pedro, two of the stars of the season, had us in control as the contest drew to a close. Michy Batshuayi, whose goal at West Brom a week earlier secured the title, added a late double as the celebrations started in earnest once more.

news.title: Erin Cuthbert: 'There will be a reaction'
news.body_en: Chelsea captain Erin Cuthbert reflected on a disappointing stalemate against Everton on Saturday afternoon, but vowed the side would bounce back against Hacken in the Women's Champions League on Tuesday. The skipper started the match for only the second time this season after recovering from a knee injury sustained in the summer and was substituted for Aggie Beever-Jones after 74 minutes with the Blues chasing a goal. Despite our best efforts, it was not to be, and Cuthbert gave her thoughts after the final whistle. She said: 'We did really well at getting ourselves ahead in the first half. That’s been our target: to score early, and then we conceded an unfortunate goal, which is no one’s fault. But we need to do a little bit more. 'We weren’t quite on the same page today defensively. We weren’t pressing as a group, as we have done in the previous games. We were a bit sloppy on the ball, too. 'But I can’t fault anybody’s effort. The effort has been there. It’s just one of those days where we were really not at it, and we can’t have too many of those if we want to be in a title race.' The teams went in with the scores at 1-1 during the interval after a Lucy Bronze own goal had cancelled out Sandy Baltimore's opener. Everton could then afford to sit back during the second half, meaning Chelsea were stuck trying to find a winner. 'You can’t get too stressed,' Cuthbert explained. 'I feel like as players we tend to look at scoreboards and things start to slip away. But you’ll always get a chance, and we had a few half-chances here and there today. We were dangerous on set pieces. We obviously scored from Katie's (McCabe) cross as well. 'But you have games where you just grind out results. You don’t always have to be at your best throughout the whole season, as long as you’re getting the results. But we didn’t have that today, and we can’t have too many more of those.' There is very little time for the team to linger over today's result, with a trip to Sweden on the horizon and a game against Hacken on Tuesday night. As captain, Cuthbert will take responsibility for lifting the spirits and making sure we are ready for that challenge, before returning to Stamford Bridge to face Manchester City next weekend. 'There’s going to be a reaction, for sure,' she said. 'There’s a lot of unhappy people in the dressing room, and rightly so, because this is a club that expects to win games of football. But just the quality was lacking for us today, myself included. If we all looked at ourselves in the dressing room, we all know that we could have done a lot better today. 'I’m sure that we’ll be back at training tomorrow, ready and fully focused on Hacken. We will make sure that we put our best foot forward come Tuesday night.'

news.title: Alonso on Lavia’s ‘brain for the team’ and his next step
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has emphasised Romeo Lavia's growing importance in his Chelsea side, highlighting the midfielder's recent development while insisting there is still more to come. Lavia was excellent in our previous two matches, against Liverpool and Manchester United, with the added bonus that he completed the 90 minutes in both. It has reinforced the belief that Lavia is establishing himself as a key controller in the heart of our midfield, and that consistency and rhythm is something Alonso knows from personal experience will only help his team. ‘I always have the feeling that every time the midfield area works, the team works better,’ Alonso said. ‘Romeo is in a very good place, not just the last game. I think that for the last month he's been very consistent in his performance. ‘He's been very important for the team because in the middle you need to have a brain for yourself, but a brain for the team. He's good with the ball, he's giving balance, and he's connecting really well with the players around him. ‘It's not rocket science to know that once you have good midfielders, the team normally looks better.’ Despite Lavia’s eye-catching displays, our manager has made it clear he will continue to demand higher standards from the Belgian international to ensure his ceiling is reached. He said: ‘We need to push him. We need to help him continue so he can take the next step, because it’s not enough yet. ‘There's been a change, and he knows that,’ added Alonso when asked if Lavia is doing anything differently. ‘He has realised that's the way.’

news.title: Frustrated Bompastor: 'We were not clinical or ruthless enough'
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor was left feeling frustrated by our 1-1 draw with Everton at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon, but felt it was an opportunity to reflect and improve before Tuesday night's Women's Champions League trip to Hacken in Sweden. The head coach said in her pre-match press conference the Toffees would be hard to break down, and that proved to be true until Sandy Baltimore broke the deadlock after 28 minutes. Yet an unfortunate own goal from Lucy Bronze levelled things up almost immediately afterwards, and Chelsea were once again forced to battle through their block. While Chelsea's unbeaten run in the WSL was extended to 17 games, and we remain undefeated in all competitions this season, Bompastor took the opportunity to reflect on the draw after the game and pointed to the areas where she felt her side were below par this afternoon. 'The result is really frustrating for us,' she said. 'Today the performance was not good enough for us to get a better result. We were probably too slow. We had 20 shots on goal, eight on target, but even when we shot on target we were not clinical enough, not ruthless enough, and I don’t think we made Everton's goalkeeper work hard enough. 'Also, the connection between the players didn’t really click today. So it happens. When we have a performance like that, it’s good for us to provide feedback and to be honest and realistic about what happened on the pitch. 'In terms of the defensive aspects, today we were not compact enough as a block. We didn’t recover enough balls in terms of the high press. So that’s something we need to do better going into the next game. 'Without the ball, we conceded an unfortunate goal, but it was the goal that allowed them to get a point from this game. So it happens sometimes. As much as we are frustrated, now it’s for us to analyse the game, take the feedback, and move on to the next one.' Despite the initial disappointment of dropping points, the head coach did point to some positives to take from the game. Chelsea kept Everton to zero shots on target throughout the 90 minutes, even if we struggled to break through their low block. And with a match against Hacken to play on Tuesday night, there's no time to dwell on today's result. 'If we analyse from the beginning of the season, we had many games where we had a lot of good performances and a lot of quality on the pitch,' she continued. 'So it’s good for us when we are doing well not to go too high and when we have a frustrating result, not to go too low. Because I believe this team has a lot of quality, and we can do better than what we did today. 'Sometimes it's good not to always perform at a good level because it means you still have work to be done, and you need that. For me, it’s best when you have a frustrating result to play quickly straight afterwards. So the quick turnaround is actually a positive thing. You can quickly move on and focus on what is next.'

news.title: Match report: Chelsea Women 1-1 Everton
news.body_en: With a defensive record only bettered by Chelsea in the WSL this season, the Blues knew we would be in for a tough afternoon against Everton even before the match had kicked off, and so it proved as we had to settle for a point at Stamford Bridge. After a cagey first half hour, Sandy Baltimore broke the deadlock when a small connection on the ball saw her steer home from a Lucy Bronze header back across goal. It felt like Chelsea were on our way, but when Bronze took an unfortunate touch from a looping ball in, the Toffees were back on level terms just four minutes later, and the teams went in at 1-1 at the break. Despite Everton not managing a shot on target during the match, the visitors made things really difficult for the Blues, reducing us to half-chances throughout. Their efforts were rewarded as they kept us from adding to the scoreline and took a point away from the Bridge. Sonia Bompastor made four alterations to her starting XI, swapping Veerle Buurman, Nathalie Bjorn and Sjoeke Nusken for Bronze, Kadeisha Buchanan and Erin Cuthbert. Lauren James had unfortunately been ruled out with a hamstring injury earlier in the week, and Wieke Kaptein came into the line-up in her place. The head coach had mentioned in her pre-match press conference that she expected the visitors to defend well, and that's exactly what happened in the opening stages of the game as the Toffees played in a compact formation as they attempted to negate our strengths. Our first real attempt came from one of Ellie Carpenter's trademark runs down the flank, and as she let fly with a shot, only a tiny deflection from the defender saw it bounce just wide of the right-hand post. Melvine Malard was next to go close with a header that was just off target, but the offside flag went up soon afterwards to confirm that it wouldn't have counted. It wasn't going to be easy to break Everton down, but the Blues were getting closer. After a superb one-two with Carpenter, Kaptein blasted her shot towards goal but had her attempt cleared off the line. Our opener came soon afterwards. After we took a short corner, Katie McCabe swung a cross into the back post to find the head of Bronze. The centre-back cushioned her header across the face of goal, allowing Baltimore to nod home with the slightest of touches. Yet the Toffees hit back when a looping cross from Yuka Momiki took an unfortunate touch off Bronze and deflected into the back of the net. Our number 22 almost cancelled out the own goal with a bullet header seven minutes before the break, but an impressive stop saw Everton goalkeeper Courtney Brosnan tip the attempt over the bar. After another tight opening to the second half, Bompastor made a double substitution after 55 minutes, introducing Nusken and Thompson for Baltimore and Kaptein. The clock ticked towards 70 and, other than a series of corners, the Blues were yet to put any real pressure on a resolute Everton defence. When the Blues were awarded a free-kick for a late challenge on Carpenter, McCabe took it short to Thompson just outside her, and the American laid the ball off to Walsh. The midfielder bent in a curling shot, but Brosnan was able to collect. That was the only real danger we caused in the second half as the statistics showed we fired 21 shots on goal but ended the match with only three big chances created. It was a frustrating day, but we will look to regain top spot when we face leaders Manchester City next weekend in the WSL. We drop to second in the table, two points behind leaders Manchester City, following their 5-0 win over West Ham United earlier today. We travel to Sweden to face Hacken in the Women's Champions League on Tuesday, with kick-off set for 5.45pm UK time. We will then back at Stamford Bridge for our top-of-the-table clash with Man City next Saturday. Tickets are still available and you can secure your place here. news.title: U18 Premier League Cup report: Chelsea Under-18s 3-1 Charlton Under-18s
news.body_en: Chelsea Under-18s are through to the quarter-finals of the U18 Premier League Cup following a 3-1 victory over Charlton Athletic. Andrew Pennie won us a spot-kick which Jashayde Greenwood coolly converted to give us the lead. Greenwood returned the favour 14 minutes later, setting up Pennie’s goal which put us back in front after Charlton’s Jayden Twum equalised in the 28th minute. The Blues pushed for a third in the second 45 minutes and our persistence soon told as we earned and converted another penalty through Greenwood. In the first half it was all Chelsea and it didn’t take long for us to take the lead. Pennie was played through on the left wing with two defenders still to beat. He cut inside, drawing a foul from the Charlton defender, leaving the referee with no choice but to point to the penalty spot. Greenwood stepped up to take and made no mistake, going hard and low into the bottom right corner while sending the goalkeeper the wrong way. The visitors responded with a goal of their own, as Twum managed to get half a yard on Jacob Hall before tucking the ball into the far corner. We regained the lead quickly, as Greenwood became the creator and Pennie the goalscorer. The former received the ball and opted to drive down towards the byline; he then cut his pass across the face of goal to Pennie, who thumped the ball against the crossbar and in to make it 2-1 before the break. After the interval, we came racing out the blocks once more, aiming to extend our advantage to ensure our spot in the last eight. We enjoyed the best opportunities of the half through Heze Grimwade and Kwamina Ampah. First, Grimwade was played through one-on-one with the goalkeeper by Greenwood but dragged his shot wide. Minutes after coming on Ampah was presented with the golden chance to settle the match as Gabriel Sambou dinked a cross into the penalty area, but Ampah’s shot was off target. Charlton put some pressure on us too, but we handled the heat well and stood firm. Josh Henry in particular denied the visitors another equaliser with two lunging challenges to turn goal-bound efforts out for a corner. The Blues eventually got their third, and it was from the spot once again as Greenwood remained composed to net his brace. We earned the penalty when Emmanuel Ayinde headed Grimwade’s cross towards goal, only to be denied by the hand of Raynon Richman. Greenwood elected for a different spot-kick approach this time; he stuttered and waited for Williams to move before smashing his strike into the opposite corner. This win means that we are through to the knockout stages of the Under-18 Premier League Cup. Chelsea Under-18s host Arsenal in the Under-18 Premier League on Saturday 21 November at Cobham Training Ground. The game gets underway at 11am GMT and supporters can watch the match live with a CFC+ subscription. news.title: Penders on learning quickly, that Mbeumo save and dreaming big
news.body_en: By his own admission, Mike Penders has experienced a ‘rollercoaster of emotions’ during his start to life between the posts at Chelsea. It is to his credit how he has handled the ups and downs thrown at him so far. Penders started the season as our number two, behind Emiliano Martinez in the pecking order. He made his Blues debut in the Carabao Cup victory over Luton Town in August and started the next round, too, as Leeds United were beaten 6-3. But the tall Belgian was thrust into the spotlight when Martinez sustained a nasty jaw injury midway through the second half of our Premier League game at Everton. Penders helped see out the clean sheet, making a positive first impression in the English top flight. However, the following weekend, it was Penders’ own goal that set Tottenham on their way to a rare victory at Stamford Bridge. That mistake was a test of the 21-year-old’s nerve, but his response was emphatic. He put in two stellar performances against Liverpool and Manchester United, with several saves plucked from the very top drawer. There is certainly plenty for Penders to reflect on as he sits down at Cobham ahead of our trip to Sunderland this weekend. ‘Right now I feel very good,’ he says. ‘It’s been a rollercoaster of emotions as well, but now I’m very happy I could react positively in the last two games. ‘When it comes to pressure, I try to stay as relaxed as possible. And then, of course, mistakes happen. You think about them, that’s normal, but I try to turn it into something positive. I try to learn about it. I like to look at the videos to see what I could do better, and then move on. ‘It was a learning moment, and outside of the mistake, I felt okay during the game. The most important thing was to have a positive reaction in the next couple of games, and I’m happy I could bring that.’ Penders benefitted from having his whole family in attendance at the Tottenham game. Afterwards, they offered support, of course, but were also able to take his mind off it by changing the subject when required. Penders also felt the love from his team-mates and his manager, Xabi Alonso. ‘He spoke very positively about me during interviews, which gave me a lot of confidence to go into the next game. Also, my defenders and some of the other players came up to me and just spoke with me. I appreciated that a lot. ‘You don’t forget these kinds of things, you know? The players who come up to you, write you a little message: "Keep your head up, keep going.” It means a lot.’ Any goalkeeper plays on the margins. A small error can be brutally punished. On the flip side, a pivotal save can preserve three points. It comes with the territory. Just seven days after his own goal, Penders made such a brilliant stop it has been nominated for the Premier League Save of the Month award. You can vote for Mike’s improbable fingertip stop from Bryan Mbeumo’s rasping volley here. It was a save so good that it needed multiple replays and camera angles to prove Penders had actually got a decisive touch on the ball. He reveals it was a source of mirth among his team-mates afterwards. ‘The ball came so quickly, I didn’t even see it properly,’ says Penders. ‘It was just instinct, pure instinct; a reaction. I felt a good touch on my fingertips, and after that moment, I screamed all the positive emotions out. I had to. I was so happy with that moment. ‘Then, after the game, no-one believed me that I touched it! I was like, “Yeah, I touched it; you will see afterwards”. ‘Then it was pretty quickly on Twitter. A team-mate came into the dressing room saying: “He touched it”. I was very happy it was a good angle because if the angle wasn't right, they could still have some doubts!’ Mike Penders' reaction time 🤯🔵 @ChelseaFC pic.twitter.com/5aXNDl8zwd Penders is flattered by comparisons to his compatriot Thibaut Courtois, which serve as motivation to work even harder. His focus now is on trying to write his own story and make a name for himself. He knows one way to do that is to learn from those around him. Martinez – ‘a very good guy’ – has already proven to be a huge help, and there are certain elements of the Argentinean’s game that Penders is trying to implement in his own, as he sees fit. Combine those Cobham learnings with invaluable Premier League experience and you sense Penders’ trajectory is rising. It gives him hope he can realise his ambitions, even if he knows there is a long way to go. ‘I have a lot of dreams...a lot of dreams. I hope I can win as many trophies as possible with the club. ‘The big dream? I think that would be winning the Champions League or winning a World Cup with my country, something like that. And then maybe go for the biggest individual prizes. ‘These are dreams that are far away, but you want to work towards them. This is the start of the journey.’

news.title: Key talking points from Sonia Bompastor's pre-Everton press conference
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor faced the media at Cobham ahead of our Women's Super League clash against Everton on Saturday, and here are the key talking points from what the Blues head coach said. We remain unbeaten this season after 13 matches, but Bompastor assured that the standard of preparation will be as high as always as we head into our fifth WSL game of the campaign at Stamford Bridge. The head coach reported that Lauren James will be missing until the end of this block of matches before the international break, after a scan confirmed that she sustained a hamstring injury during the 6-0 win over Charlton last weekend. Lexi Potter, meanwhile, is available again. Here are the rest of the key talking points from our head coach’s pre-match press conference on Friday. 'My role is to make sure that when we are in good form, we don't go too high. And sometimes when things are not going the way we want, we don't go too low either. I'm responsible for that. 'Right now, of course, we are happy with the results and most of the performances we are having on the pitch, but we won't change anything. We keep working hard, we keep the same mentality, we train with intensity, and we come into every game as well prepared as we can. 'That's what we need to do. Every game in this league is so important and so difficult, so we need to make sure we sustain that for as long as possible.' 'It's always difficult to score goals against any team. The difference maybe in the Charlton game was that we scored early on the game, and we were winning 4-0 after 19 minutes. And when you are really efficient and clinical from the beginning, it changes the whole game. 'Going into the game tomorrow, we are expecting it might not be possible for us to achieve. They are a really difficult team to break down, and we will have to play at our best if we want to get a result from the game. We'll try our best to break them down, to score as early as possible in the game and to see how they react. 'They haven't conceded many goals, and they are an aggressive team, but in a good way. They had a good result against Manchester United, so I'm sure they are coming in with confidence as well. We are very much aware of the threats and the quality this Everton side has, especially in terms of the defensive aspects.' 'It's really important to be hungry. The hunger is part of the mentality and the mindset a team have, and that's what makes the difference between the good teams and the great teams, the ones who are able to win trophies. 'Sometimes you don't always play the best football, but you always find a way to win games, and that's really important. We focus a lot on the quality of the performance we want to put on the pitch, but some days it's not always possible for different reasons. We need to make sure when those days come, we have that hunger and that mentality to turn things around even when it's not the way we want to play.' 'Ellie has been starting her actions higher up the pitch for sure, and also she probably feels more freedom to attack. She's been working really hard in training sessions, and she stays at the end to do some extra work around finishing in the box, crosses, the quality of the crosses, scanning, and the quality of her first touch. 'She's always keen to work hard, and she always asks for extras. She's been doing that from the beginning of the season, and it's paying off, so it's good for her.' 'Everyone could see that it was Lucy (Bronze). She was really good at scaring people. She got me, but she also got most people in the team. But it was really nice. 'We work really hard most of the time, and we spend so much time focusing on every detail. We speak a lot about our ambitions, how we want to perform on the pitch, and we are professional, so we do that one hundred per cent. 'But it's also good when you can find a good balance and have good laughs and some fun. At the end of the day, football is a game, and when your team is able to play at their best, it's when players have fun on the pitch.' See the Blues in action against Everton at Stamford Bridge tomorrow! Tickets are available here...

news.title: Alonso wants Chelsea focused on the pitch, not the table
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso insists it is still much too early to be reading anything from the Premier League table, both in terms of his Chelsea team’s progress and the quality of opponent we will face against Sunderland. The Blues head to the Stadium of Light for our next Premier League fixture, taking on Sunderland in a 2pm kick-off on Sunday. A quick glance at the league table would suggest the two teams go into the game in very different fortunes. With three wins from our four Premier League matches since the last international break, Chelsea sit fourth in the table, with a chance to move up to third this weekend. Meanwhile, the Black Cats are stuck in the bottom spot, with just one league win to their name in 2026/27. However, our manager insisted he isn’t thinking about the league table at this stage of the campaign, when asked in his pre-match press conference if Chelsea’s position was a sign of our progress so far this season under his leadership. ‘The table means not too much because that can change so much in one week, in two games,’ Alonso pointed out. ‘We are taking a step forward, I think, with the ball, against the ball, being more solid. ‘We have a tough opponent, a tough visit to Sunderland, we know what it takes to win there. We know how demanding it will be. ‘The table doesn’t matter. I think that they deserve more points than they’ve got and it's going to be a tough away game.’ Instead, it is the task of building the consistency and momentum needed to be challenging in the upper reaches of the Premier League come May which is taking up Alonso and his team’s attention. That continues at Sunderland on Sunday, when the Blues will attempt to follow up last week’s 2-0 victory over Manchester United by making it back-to-back wins in the Premier League. ‘As I've said, it’s early days to talk too much about the table. We won the last game, now the focus is to keep winning, winning, winning and to build this mentality to go game by game. ‘We are expecting a tough game on Sunday against a team that do many good things. They should have more points probably and it is not going to be easy, for sure.’

news.title: Highlights: Chelsea U18s vs Charlton U18s
Sunderland vs Chelsea: All you need to know
news.body_en: With almost a quarter of the Premier League campaign completed, fourth-placed Chelsea travel to the Stadium of Light. Club historian Rick Glanvill and club statistician Paul Dutton look ahead to Sunday's 2pm kick-off against Sunderland. It will be the Blues’ first appearance in this time slot since our 4-3 beating of Brighton & Hove Albion and is a consequence of the Black Cats’ UEFA Europa League involvement on Thursday. Ebullient when Chelsea lost 2-1 there in May, Sunderland supporters are nervy in November, with five losses in six league outings and no three-point haul since August. As the final international break of 2026 looms, they lie bottom of the Premier League pile, two points from safety with the second-worst goal difference in the division. For their Europa League game in midweek, Regis Le Bris rotated six of the 11 who started last weekend’s 3-1 loss to fellow relegation fighters Coventry City. Previously unbeaten in the competition, they lost 2-0 at home to Dinamo Zagreb. Meanwhile, Xabi Alonso’s team had a free midweek to rest and prepare, following Saturday's second-half 2-0 dismantling of Manchester United, and will rise to third with a win on Wearside, should Brighton fail to beat Brentford. Speaking in his pre-match press conference, Alonso revealed that he will make a late decision on Sunday to determine if Moises Caicedo and Emiliano Martinez have recovered sufficiently to feature against Sunderland. Jorrel Hato, Maxence Lacroix and Joao Pedro remain unavailable until at least the end of the forthcoming international break. ‘On Saturday we have our last training session before Sunday and we will decide,' Alonso replied when asked about Martinez. 'But he is training well. It is very good that Emi has made a great effort to be back and is ahead of the plan to be part of the team. So we will check and then on Sunday we will take the final decision. ‘Moi had little problems after the last game, so we expect to check on Saturday on different situations and he is one of them.' It may surprise Chelsea fans scarred by historic cup losses at Sunderland to hear that the Blues have a decent league record there. We have won 34 per cent of our 61 trips to this part of the North-East, just four fewer than our 38 per cent success rate at Tottenham Hotspur. Even before Roker Park closed its turnstiles in 1997, Chelsea had enjoyed sporadic success there, including a classic 2-0 victory in which Mickey Thomas scored from the spot soon after the restart and Kerry Dixon sealed the points late on. That was the first time we had ever won at Roker by two or more goals and remains our joint-biggest margin of victory at Sunderland. A run of just one top-flight defeat and no draws against the Black Cats between 2002 and 2013 weighs in heavily on that wins statistic, and the sole loss in that run came at Stamford Bridge. The spree of nine straight wins at the Stadium of Light included two memorably high-scoring clashes. A goalless first half did not foretell what was to happen after the break there on the last day of the 2008/09 season, a week before Guus Hiddink’s men would beat Everton in the FA Cup final. Nicolas Anelka broke the deadlock early in the second half with a spectacular drive from distance (to secure the Golden Boot), before Kieran Richardson made Petr Cech pay for a rare mishandling. The game swung again when Salomon Kalou lashed into the corner and Ashley Cole netted his second for the club to make it 3-1.  In the last minute, Kenwyne Jones pulled another one back for the relegation-threatened Wearsiders, and news filtered through that Newcastle United had lost to Aston Villa and would suffer the drop instead. Two years later, in February 2011, Phil Bardsley’s solo effort struck an early blow for the hosts, but minutes later Ahmed Elmohamady fouled Cole and Frank Lampard equalised from 12 yards. Anelka then pounced on a loose ball to feed Kalou, who edged Carlo Ancelotti’s defending champions ahead for the first time. The Black Cats kept scrapping and Richardson fired a free-kick through the Blues’ wall to send the two teams in level at the break. Chelsea continued to pepper Craig Gordon’s goal and when the keeper parried Lampard’s lashed shot, John Terry forced it home.  Before the final whistle, Anelka struck to seal an impressive 4-2 victory. Our most recent win at the home of the Mackems came in mid-December 2016, under Antonio Conte. The league leaders remained top over Christmas for the fifth time in the Premier League, thanks to Cesc Fabregas’ swept finish. Following his success against Manchester United, Cole Palmer has scored 19 of his 21 Premier League penalties for Chelsea. Only Frank Lampard (41 from 48) has managed a higher total. Romeo Lavia won possession 14 times during Saturday’s win, the most by any Chelsea player in a Premier League game since Lewis Hall against Fulham in January 2023 (also 14). Alonso’s side are outperforming the expected goals (13.34) metric by +5.56 (19 goals), the second best in the Premier League, while Sunderland are underperforming theirs (13.21) by -6.21, the second-worst performers. Chelsea have won 54.7 per cent of ground duels, the highest rate in the top flight. Only five teams have a lower pass completion rate this season than Sunderland (78.8 per cent). Chelsea (six) have found the net more times from set-plays in the league than any rival except Brighton (seven). The Blues (53) have managed the most shots on target in the Premier League, but also sustained the most by opponents (50). The Black Cats have not won at home in the top flight on this date since 1932, when they beat Grimsby 3-2. A year earlier, in a 2-0 defeat at Roker Park, Chelsea fielded our oldest-ever starting XI, averaging 31 years and 336 days.

Xabi Alonso delivers latest on Caicedo and Anselmino fitness
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has issued an update on the fitness of Moises Caicedo and Aaron Anselmino ahead of this weekend’s Premier League trip to Sunderland. The Blues manager confirmed earlier today (Friday) in his pre-match press conference that he will wait until after our final session tomorrow to make a call on Caicedo, who was absent from training earlier this week. Alonso said the Ecuadorian was feeling discomfort because of ‘little problems’ in the wake of our victory over Manchester United. He has, however, confirmed Caicedo has been out on the grass at points this week. ‘He’s doing bits and other bits,’ said Alonso, reiterating that a decision will be made on the 25-year-old's fitness after the final training session. Alonso has positive news on Anselmino, who has been called up to the Argentina national squad alongside Emiliano Martinez and Valentin Barco. The defender has yet to make his Chelsea debut, but there is a possibility that could change this weekend at the Stadium of Light. ‘He’s doing everything, and tomorrow [Saturday] we’ll decide, but he could be in the squad, yes,' said Alonso. 'They (Argentina) asked us and he has been training better for the last ten days, and it’s very important for him have this first call-up.'
